references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the selection of the twelve apostles, where Jesus called his twelve disciples and gave them authority.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus went up on the mountain and called to himself those he wanted, and chose twelve whom he also named apostles.
The preceding verse stating that Jesus spent the whole night in prayer to God, which is the immediate context before the selection of the twelve.
The following list of the names of the twelve apostles whom Jesus chose.
Jesus says that he has chosen the twelve, emphasizing the deliberate choice (ἐκλεξάμενος) of the twelve disciples.
Jesus tells the disciples: "You did not choose me, but I chose you", reflecting that it was Jesus who actively selected the apostles.
Luke refers back to Jesus giving command to the apostles he had chosen through the Holy Spirit—a clear connection to the selection in Luke 6:13.
The list of the eleven apostles gathered in Jerusalem after the ascension, showing continuity from the selection in Luke 6:13.
Paul describes how Christ gave some as apostles, others as prophets, and so on—this connects to Jesus' sovereign choice of apostles.
The wall of the new Jerusalem has twelve foundations bearing the names of the Lamb's twelve apostles, showing the lasting significance of the selection of the twelve.
